steps.what: Find and read the actual approved research protocol, consultation scope and existing method guidance for developing intervention procedures in {DOCS}.

Existing approved protocol and method sources

Existing protocol and consent conditions from s1

Actual consultation evidence from s2
Existing consent and research boundaries

Actual observed interaction and context from s3

Actual supporting evidence notes from s3b

tasks.design: Configure native approved-protocol/method views. Retain real interviews, consultations, participant observation, field-note capture, intervention reasoning and substantive procedure writing. Save the completed checked document separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: A small amount of repeated approved-method and protocol navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Context, trust, conflicting accounts and consequences of an intervention.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret actual interaction and develop locally meaningful procedures.

ambition.what: No automatic intervention selection or implementation.

tasks.altitude: Very small retrieval gain; actual research and procedure design remain human.

reach.learn: Separate observed evidence from the proposed intervention

evidence.claim: Native method-source views can shorten navigation without replacing interviews, participant observation or intervention judgment.

assumptions: Shares are conditional E1 active-work estimates, not measured research baselines. Actual field notes and written procedure are included separately from dialogue and observation. This is procedure development, not clinical treatment or intervention implementation.

Existing protocol owners supply current approved documents. The anthropologist produces actual interview evidence in s2, actual observations in s3, separate factual field-note capture in s3b, and actual procedure decisions in s4. No free transcript, participant profile or structured evidence feed is assumed.

Native views come first; missing protocol details require manual clarification. No model analysis of participants or automatic cultural/behavioural judgment. No saving on original evidence capture, new procedure content, final checking or same-system save.

The ordinary completed-document check supplies the requested save gate without new self-approval labour; changed content requires rechecking. Consultation itself makes no binding implementation commitment. Existing method and consent controls remain fully counted; no extra approval ceremony is invented.

tasks.short: Improve curriculum cultural sensitivity with educators

steps.what: Obtain and read the actual elementary or secondary curriculum and relevant existing classroom materials in the authorised educator workspace {DOCS}.
inputs: Actual educator request
Existing curriculum and classroom materials
outputs: Actual current materials and teaching context

steps.what: Examine actual classroom interaction and discuss contextual concerns with educators and teachers, avoiding assumptions about pupils based on cultural group labels.
inputs: Actual classroom context and materials from s1
Actual educator observations and concerns
outputs: Actual contextual observations and issues for collaborative consideration

steps.what: Collaborate with educators and teachers to enhance cultural sensitivity through actual curriculum and classroom-interaction changes, agreeing specific reasoning and limits.
inputs: Actual materials from s1
Actual contextual evidence from s2
Educators' actual instructional constraints
outputs: Actual collaboratively developed change proposals and rationale

steps.what: Write the actual agreed curriculum revisions and classroom-interaction guidance in {DOCS}, using existing headings and source-reference fields while authoring substantive changes personally.
inputs: Actual agreed proposals and rationale from s3
Actual original materials from s1
outputs: Complete curriculum/guidance draft with visible changes and limitations

steps.what: Check and correct the complete final curriculum and interaction-guidance draft against actual collaboration, context, wording, confidentiality and intended educator recipients.
inputs: Complete draft from s4
Actual original materials and agreed changes
outputs: Exact checked final proposed materials and recipients

steps.what: Save the exact checked final proposed curriculum and guidance in {DOCS}.
inputs: Exact completed proposed materials checked in s5
outputs: Saved final proposal

steps.what: Send the exact checked proposed curriculum and classroom guidance to the designated educators through {EMAIL}.
inputs: Unchanged final proposal saved in s6
Recipients checked in s5
outputs: Actual educator-delivered proposal

tasks.design: Use native current-material views and document headings/reference fields. Retain real contextual examination, collaboration and substantive curricular changes; provide the actual completed checked proposal through a separate delivery step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated source navigation and proposal presentation work around substantive educator collaboration.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document views and reusable headings/reference fields.
tasks.still_hard: Local meaning, exclusion and what changes help actual classroom interaction.
tasks.human_edge: Listen to educators and evaluate context without stereotyping pupils.

ambition.what: No automatic pupil classification or curriculum adoption.

tasks.altitude: Small clerical reduction with contextual and educational judgments retained.

reach.learn: Use actual collaboration rather than cultural stereotypes

evidence.claim: Native views and document fields can reduce navigation and presentation without determining cultural sensitivity.

assumptions: Shares are E1 conditional active-work estimates, not measured consulting baselines. Actual classroom context, collaboration, substantive revised materials and delivery are included. No generic culture profile or pupil scoring is created.

Educators supply actual existing curriculum through unchanged work. The anthropologist obtains context in s1-s2 and actual collaborative proposals in s3 before writing in s4. No free recorded classroom stream, automated surveillance or assumed consensus.

Test native features before custom code. s4 shortens only headings and reference placement, not new educational content. If those features already exist, their saving is zero. Educators retain actual curriculum adoption and classroom practice; no saving in their unchanged work is claimed.

Ordinary completed-proposal checking supplies requested save and send gates without extra self-approval labour. Any changed content or recipient requires renewed checking. Both short save and send steps remain fully retained with no saving.
research_questions: Can native proposal fields reduce presentation effort while preserving the exact locally agreed changes?

Unchanged final proposal and educator recipients checked in s5

steps.what: Interpret the actual archival evidence to help explain origins and development of cultural patterns, considering contradictory material and limits of the surviving collection.

Archive staff supply existing catalogue descriptions and actual materials through unchanged work. The researcher locates sources in s1, produces actual observations in s2 and actual interpretation in s3 before recording in s4. No free OCR, handwriting transcription or newly digitised collection is assumed.

Native catalogue configuration comes first. Missing descriptions, physical access or unreadable material require manual work; those cases receive no navigation gain. No saving on original reading, cultural reasoning, new factual research notes or the short same-system save.

The ordinary completed-note check supplies the requested save gate without additional self-approval labour; any changed source passage or interpretation requires rechecking. Already configured filters yield zero new gain.

tasks.short: Formulate theories of cultures and social institutions

inputs: Actual theoretical research question
Existing published and authorised research records
outputs: Original relevant studies and evidence records

steps.what: Critically examine the actual comparative evidence, study methods, historical context and contradictory cases before generalising about cultures and social institutions.

outputs: Researcher's actual comparison, uncertainties and limits

steps.what: Formulate actual proposed general rules describing and predicting cultural or institutional development and behavior, specifying mechanisms, scope and falsifiable implications.

outputs: Researcher's actual theoretical propositions and stated scope

tasks.design: Configure current-study and source views in the authorised research library. Retain actual evidence criticism, theory formation, counterexample testing and the substantive theoretical document. Save the finished checked document separately.

tasks.still_hard: Whether a proposed cultural generalisation is defensible and genuinely predictive.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise contextual exceptions, rival explanations and overgeneralisation.

evidence.claim: Native source views can reduce literature navigation without validating general rules about social institutions.

assumptions: Shares are E1 conditional active-work estimates, not measured theory-development baselines. Actual theoretical propositions and the written argument are included. This is formulation of general research claims, not an operational prediction or classification service.

Source researchers produce existing studies and records through unchanged work. The anthropologist retrieves them in s1, produces actual critical comparison in s2 and actual propositions in s3-s4 before writing in s5. No structured cross-cultural dataset, new statistical analysis or measured predictive accuracy is invented.

Native source views come first. Missing evidence requires manual research and explicit uncertainty, not generated facts. No saving on substantive reading, theoretical creation, counterexample reasoning, new written arguments or same-system save. Already configured retrieval gives zero new gain.

The ordinary completed-argument check supplies the requested save gate without extra self-approval labour. Any later revision requires renewed checking. Publication and peer review are separate unchanged processes with no automatic submission assumed.
